newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ELAHI'S 89 SETS PAKISTAN ON WAY TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELAHI'S 89 SETS PAKISTAN ON WAY TO VICTORY.

text.p: Opening batsman Zahoor Elahi hit a dashing 89 but Pakistan then had to recover from a middle-order batting collapse to beat Tasmania by three wickets in a limited overs tour match on Sunday.
Elahi's innings proved decisive as Pakistan slumped midway through their chase for Tasmania's total of 235 for six from 50 overs.

Pakistan reached 236 for seven from 49 overs despite losing four wickets for 17 after Elahi got the tourists off to a flying start in valuable partnerships with opening partner Shahid Afridi and number three batsman Mohammad Wasim.
Pakistan had appeared set for an easy victory in reaching 161 for two after innings of 28 by Afridi and 39 by Wasim.

Medium-pacer Daniel Marsh prompted the collapse, bowling Inzamam-ul-Haq for four and ending Zahoor's innings in the same fashion after the Pakistani opener had hit 13 boundaries from the 108 deliveries he faced.
All-rounder Shaun Young had Pakistan captain Wasim Akram caught by Michael Farrell for six before wicketkeeper Moin Khan steadied the innings with 19 as Pakistan reached 203 for seven.
A resolute stand of 33 between spinners Saqlain Mushtaq and Mushtaq Ahmed saw Pakistan home, Saqlain Mushtaq hitting 23 in almost even time and Mushtaq Ahmed making 15.

Earlier, Young gave Tasmania cause for hope with a brisk, undefeated innings of 59 from 61 balls against a depleted Pakistan attack. Pace bowler Waqar Younis, still recovering from a nagging shoulder injury, was named 12th man.

Deposed test batsman Ricky Ponting started promisingly before falling to Shahid for 22. Ponting was dropped by Australia selectors for the third test against West Indies late last month and is attempting to regain his place for the fourth test starting in Adelaide on January 25.
